prompt.context: Our client is a national shipping company that focuses on ground transportation of commercial freight. For the past 15 years, it has been using diesel engines to power its fleet of vehicles, but now wants to explore the possibility of switching to electric powered engines (EV technology) due to rising fuel costs. The CEO has approached us for guidance and wants to know how to proceed.
prompt.question: Should our client switch its fleet of vehicles from diesel engines to electric vehicle (EV) technology, and if so, how should they proceed?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have in-house EV capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: No. The client has identified a third-party supplier to provide the EV technology. Assume the current supplier offers the best EV opportunity in terms of price and efficiency.

clarifying_info.q: Will the client buy new vehicles or retrofit existing ones?
clarifying_info.a: Since it has an extensive fleet, the client wants to retro-fit existing vehicles rather than buying new ones.

clarifying_info.q: Has any competitor adopted EV technology?
clarifying_info.a: No other ground transportation company has used EV powered engines. If the client proceeds, it will be the first in the industry to do so.

clarifying_info.q: What is the fuel efficiency improvement from EV?
clarifying_info.a: EV technology has the potential to double existing fuel efficiency.

clarifying_info.q: What are the current fleet costs?
clarifying_info.a: Number of vehicles: 2,000; Cost of fuel per gallon: $3.00; Fuel tank size: 50 gallons; Average miles travelled per week: 1,000; Average mpg: 10; Average annual maintenance and repair: $500; Insurance: $1,000/year; Labor: $20,000/year.

clarifying_info.q: What will costs look like after EV conversion?
clarifying_info.a: Number of vehicles: 2,000; Cost of fuel per gallon: $3.00; Fuel tank size: 50 gallons; Average miles travelled per week: 1,000; Average mpg: 20; Average annual maintenance and repair: $3,500; Insurance: $3,000/year; Labor: $20,000/year.

clarifying_info.q: What does the EV retrofit cost per vehicle?
clarifying_info.a: The retrofit cost is $5,000 per vehicle.

clarifying_info.q: What is the remaining useful life of the current vehicles?
clarifying_info.a: The current vehicles have a remaining useful life of 10 years.

framework: Diesel engine costs vs. EV technology costs — compare all cost components side by side
Initial costs: cost of retrofitting each vehicle
Fuel costs: current vs. future mpg, cost per gallon, miles driven
Maintenance and repair costs: current vs. future (EV likely higher as new technology)
Insurance costs: current vs. future (higher premium for untested technology)
Switching benefits: net cost savings over vehicle lifetime; positive brand/ESG positioning as first EV adopter in industry
Switching hurdles: efficacy of untested technology; limited EV recharging infrastructure on highways; vehicle downtime during retrofitting; supplier negotiation risk; unanticipated costs

questions.prompt: Calculate the current and future annual fuel costs per vehicle, and the annual fuel savings per vehicle.
questions.guidance: Strong answer walks through miles per tank, fill-ups per week, weekly cost, then annualizes. Bonus for recognizing that doubling mpg halves fuel cost directly.

math.setup: Current: mpg=10, tank=50 gal, miles/week=1000, fuel price=$3.00/gal. Future: mpg=20.
steps: Current miles per tank = 10 mpg * 50 gal = 500 miles
Current fill-ups per week = 1000 miles / 500 miles = 2
Future miles per tank = 20 mpg * 50 gal = 1,000 miles
Future fill-ups per week = 1000 miles / 1000 miles = 1

questions.prompt: Calculate the total annual costs per vehicle under diesel and under EV, the annual savings per vehicle, and the total net savings for the entire fleet over the vehicles' remaining useful life.
questions.guidance: Strong answer tallies all four cost lines for each scenario, computes per-vehicle annual saving, then multiplies by remaining useful life and subtracts retrofit cost, then scales to full fleet. Bonus for mentioning time value of money / NPV.

math.setup: Fleet: 2,000 vehicles. Remaining useful life: 10 years. Retrofit cost: $5,000/vehicle.
steps: Current total annual cost per vehicle = $15,000 (fuel) + $500 (maintenance) + $20,000 (labor) + $1,000 (insurance) = $36,500
Future total annual cost per vehicle = $7,500 (fuel) + $3,500 (maintenance) + $20,000 (labor) + $3,000 (insurance) = $34,000
Net saving per vehicle after retrofit = $25,000 - $5,000 = $20,000
math.answer: $40M net savings for the fleet over the remaining vehicle lifetime

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and hurdles should the client consider before committing to the EV conversion?

categories.name: Technology risk
ideas: Client would be first in commercial ground freight to adopt EV — effectiveness is untested at this scale
Vehicles must travel 1,000 miles per week; current EV technology is typically limited to shorter ranges
Battery range anxiety on long-haul or highway routes

categories.name: Infrastructure risk
ideas: Limited EV recharging stations, especially on highways and in sparsely populated areas
Need to establish or negotiate access to charging infrastructure along routes

categories.name: Operational risk
ideas: Vehicle downtime during the retrofitting process disrupts normal transportation operations
Drivers may need retraining on EV operation

categories.name: Financial / supplier risk
ideas: Unanticipated costs in deploying new technology at scale
Dependence on a single third-party EV supplier — limited leverage in negotiations
Higher insurance premiums for untested technology may increase over time

categories.name: Maintenance risk
ideas: Repair and maintenance network for EV components is sparse, especially on highways
Mechanics may lack EV expertise; new training or contractors needed

recommendation: Our client should proceed with retrofitting its fleet to EV technology, as the conversion is expected to save $40M over the remaining 10-year useful life of the vehicles after accounting for the $5,000 per-vehicle retrofit cost.
risks: First-mover risk: no other ground transporter has used EV, so commercial effectiveness is unproven
Range limitations: current EV technology may not reliably support 1,000-mile weekly routes
Infrastructure gap: limited recharging stations on highways and in rural areas
Unanticipated costs: new technology may carry hidden expenses not captured in the model
next_steps: Work with the EV supplier to pilot-test technology effectiveness before full rollout
Run a pilot program with a small subset of vehicles to validate costs and operational impact
Gather feedback from drivers on EV performance and range adequacy
Research government incentives or tax credits for EV fleet adoption
Investigate whether EV adoption could expand the customer base or justify premium pricing on green shipping services
Assess whether EV adoption grows customer base or revenue through ESG positioning
